response.value: I’m reviewing the feature notes and the existing requirements so I can surface only the real ambiguities beyond the already-decided decisions.

1. Ambiguity: Is the approval threshold checked with exact decimal arithmetic and is the boundary inclusive? Why it matters: “up to 50,000” and “up to 500,000” can be interpreted as either inclusive or exclusive, and decimal handling matters around cents. Recommended default: Use Decimal comparisons with inclusive boundaries, so 50,000 and 500,000 are valid, and anything above 500,000 requires the second director approval.

2. Ambiguity: What counts as “above 500,000” when values are stored as decimals or currency? Why it matters: A value like 500,000.00, 500,000.01, and 500,000.0001 can create different approval outcomes depending on rounding. Recommended default: Compare the exact invoice amount as a Decimal with no rounding before policy evaluation; only values strictly greater than 500,000 require two approvers.

3. Ambiguity: What defines “same user” when approving the same invoice? Why it matters: The same person could be entered with different casing or formatting; if IDs are compared too literally, the system could incorrectly allow duplicate approvals. Recommended default: Normalize the approver identifier to a canonical form such as trimmed and case-insensitive before comparing, and treat the same normalized value as the same user.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Conventions

- Controllers live in `Controllers/`, one per resource, route `api/[controller]`. Request bodies are `record` types declared inside the controller.
- Controllers inherit `ApiControllerBase` and use `Handle(...)` so service errors map to 404, 409 and 400.
- Every endpoint is behind sign-in. Restrict actions with `[RequireRole("...")]`: destructive actions are Admin only, approvals are Approver or Admin.
- Business rules go in the Domain project, never in controllers.
- Register services in `Program.cs`. Repositories are interfaces in Domain with an in-memory implementation in Api.
- Every new rule or endpoint needs tests. Use `FakeInvoiceRepository` in tests.
- Use clear names; no one-letter variables or `flag` parameters.
- End-to-end tests use page objects and role-based locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`), never CSS or XPath selectors.

## Commands

- Run the app: `dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api` then open http://localhost:5000
- Run the tests: `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln`
- Run end-to-end tests: `cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm test`

## Demo accounts (not real credentials)

- `demo.approver` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Approver)
- `demo.admin` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Admin)

## Never

- Commit real credentials, tokens or customer data.
- Add business logic to `Program.cs` or controllers.

## Feature: approval limits by role (OpenSpec change: add-role-approval-limits)
### Rules (amounts are decimal; limits are inclusive)
- Manager may approve alone when Amount <= 50,000.
- Director may approve alone when Amount <= 500,000.
- Amount > 500,000 needs two approvals from two different users. The first approver must be a
Manager or Director. The second approver must be a Director.
- After the first approval of an invoice above 500,000 the invoice stays Pending with one entry in
its approvals list. Only the second valid approval makes it Approved.
- The same user id never counts twice on one invoice. Compare ids case-insensitively.
- Admin and every other role cannot approve. The seeded user demo.approver becomes a Manager.
New seeded users: demo.director and demo.director2. <adjust to recon if needed>
- A rejected attempt returns a reason code and a human-readable message and changes NOTHING on the
invoice: not the status, not the approvals list, not any timestamp.
- Reason codes: NotAnApprover, ExceedsApprovalLimit, RequiresTwoApprovers (interim only),
SameApprover, SecondApproverMustBeDirector, InvalidState (map to existing not-pending behaviour).
- If several rejections apply, report the first of: InvalidState, NotAnApprover,
ExceedsApprovalLimit, SameApprover, SecondApproverMustBeDirector.
- Out of scope, do not add: creator-cannot-approve, currency, delegation, audit log, persistence.
### Layering for this feature
- Domain: a pure ApprovalPolicy (no I/O, no mutation) and an ApprovalService that calls the policy
first and mutates the invoice only after the policy accepted. Limits are named constants in one
place only.
- API: controllers only map the result to HTTP using the existing error handling. No business rules
in controllers.
- UI: show the rejection message in an element with role="alert".
### Tests
- Unit test command: <from recon, e.g. dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln>
- E2E command: cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm test
- Tests are written from the spec scenarios, not from reading the implementation.
- Every rule needs boundary tests at 50,000 / 50,000.01 / 500,000 / 500,000.01.
- After every rejection a test asserts the invoice equals its snapshot from before the call.
- Assert reason codes, not message text.
### Review expectations
- Every review finding has: severity, file, line, finding, suggested fix.
- Every finding on the pull request gets one verdict: fixed (with commit), dismissed (with reason),
or deferred (with reason and issue link).
- Never commit code you have not read. Never claim tests pass without running them.
### Git conventions
- Branch: feature/role-approval-limits. One logical change per commit. The message says what
changed and why.

## Agents, skills and output format
- Agents (.github/agents): feature-lead (delegates to subagents), spec-writer, implementer,
test-writer, reviewer.
- Skills (.github/skills): approval-rules, write-approval-tests, pr-review, run-mutation-testing.
- Logging: hooks in .github/hooks append every prompt and tool call to docs/ai-log/ai-interactions.jsonl.
- Agents never commit. A human reads every diff and commits.
- Reviews go to docs/reviews/review-<n>.json in the schema defined in the pr-review skill; a hook
validates the format after every tool call.
### Output format (all agents)
End every reply with exactly one line:
RESULT: <done|blocked> | FILES: <comma-separated paths, or none> | NEXT: <one sentence>

# Invoice approval role limits

## Scope

This capability covers approval limits by role, non-approver rejection, distinct-approver enforcement, and unchanged-invoice behavior for rejected attempts.

All scenarios assume the invoice status is Pending unless stated otherwise.

## T1: Manager approves 50,000.00
WHEN the invoice amount is 50,000.00 and the current user is a Manager
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice becomes Approved.

## T2: Manager approves 50,000.01
WHEN the invoice amount is 50,000.01 and the current user is a Manager
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code ExceedsApprovalLimit
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## T3: Manager approves 1.00
WHEN the invoice amount is 1.00 and the current user is a Manager
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice becomes Approved.

## T4: Director approves 50,000.01
WHEN the invoice amount is 50,000.01 and the current user is a Director
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice becomes Approved.

## T5: Director approves 500,000.00
WHEN the invoice amount is 500,000.00 and the current user is a Director
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice becomes Approved.

## T7: Admin approves any invoice
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and the current user is an Admin
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code NotAnApprover
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## T8: Manager approves an invoice that is not Pending
WHEN the invoice status is Draft and the current user is a Manager
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code InvalidState
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## T9: User without an approver role approves
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and the current user has no approver role
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code NotAnApprover
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## U1: First Director approval above 500,000 stays Pending
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and user A is a Director and this is the first approval on the invoice
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice stays Pending
AND approvals contains exactly [A].

## U2: Second Director approval completes the invoice
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and user A has already approved and user B is a Director and user B approves next
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice becomes Approved
AND approvals contains exactly [A, B].

## U3: Same user approves twice
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and user A has already approved and user A approves again
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code SameApprover
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## U4: Same user id differs only by case
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and user id "alice" has already approved and user id "ALICE" approves next
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code SameApprover
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## U5: Non-director second approver is rejected
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and user A has already approved and user M is a Manager and M approves next
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code SecondApproverMustBeDirector
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## U6: Same approver precedence over second-approver rule
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and user M is the first approver and user M attempts to approve again
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code SameApprover
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## U7: Manager as first approver above 500,000
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and user M is a Manager and this is the first approval on the invoice
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice stays Pending
AND approvals contains exactly [M].

## U8: Valid Director approval after a rejected second attempt
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and a rejected second attempt has already occurred for the same invoice and user B is a Director
THEN the next valid Director approval is accepted and the invoice becomes Approved
AND approvals contains the valid prior approver and B.

## U9: Director approves 500,000.00 alone
WHEN the invoice amount is 500,000.00 and the current user is a Director
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice becomes Approved.

## U10: Director approves 500,000.01 as first approval
WHEN the invoice amount is 500,000.01 and the current user is a Director and no prior approval exists
THEN the approval is accepted and the invoice stays Pending
AND approvals contains exactly [current user].

## U11: Admin cannot approve first above 500,000
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and the current user is an Admin
THEN the approval is rejected with reason code NotAnApprover
AND approvals remains empty.

## U12: Third approval attempt after approval is invalid
WHEN the invoice amount is 600,000.00 and the invoice is already Approved
THEN any further approval attempt is rejected with reason code InvalidState
AND the invoice is unchanged.

## Rejection precedence
WHEN several rejection conditions can apply at once
THEN the system resolves the first applicable reason in this order: InvalidState, NotAnApprover, ExceedsApprovalLimit, SameApprover, SecondApproverMustBeDirector.

# Design: add-role-approval-limits

## Layering

- The domain owns the approval policy as a pure decision component. It receives the invoice, the acting user, and the requested approval context, and it returns either an accepted decision or a rejection reason.
- The `ApprovalService` orchestrates the flow: it checks invoice state, calls the policy, and only mutates the invoice after the policy accepts the change.
- Controllers remain thin and map domain results to HTTP responses using the existing error-handling pattern. They do not contain business rules.
- The UI displays rejection messages in an alert element and does not own the policy logic.

## Data change

- The invoice model must carry an `Approvals` list so that approval events are recorded per invoice.
- Each approval entry identifies the user who approved; the list is compared by user id, case-insensitively, to prevent duplicate approval counting.
- For amounts above 500,000, the first valid approval keeps the invoice Pending and records one approval. The second valid director approval completes the invoice.
- Rejected attempts leave the invoice object unchanged, including state, approval list, and timestamps.

## Error mapping

- InvalidState maps to the existing not-pending approval behaviour.
- NotAnApprover maps to authorization-style rejection when the acting user lacks an approver role.
- ExceedsApprovalLimit maps to the single-approver role limit failure on the amount-based path.
- SameApprover maps to duplicate approval attempts from the same user.
- SecondApproverMustBeDirector maps to a non-director attempt on the second approval step.

## Rejection precedence

The policy must evaluate reasons in the following order and stop at the first one that applies:

1. InvalidState
2. NotAnApprover
3. ExceedsApprovalLimit
4. SameApprover
5. SecondApproverMustBeDirector

This ordering ensures deterministic behavior and stable tests regardless of which multiple conditions are true.

## 1.x Phase 1: single-approver limits
- [ ] Roles and seed users: demo.approver becomes Manager; add Director users; confirm Admin cannot approve.
- [ ] ApprovalPolicy implements the single-approver limits by role and the rejection reasons.
- [ ] ApprovalService orchestrates validation and state mutation after the policy accepts.
- [ ] API error mapping converts approval rejections into existing HTTP/error behavior.
- [ ] Unit tests T1 to T9 cover the single-approver scenarios and unchanged-invoice assertions.
- [ ] UI message for rejections is displayed in an alert element.
- [ ] Interim rule T6: Director approves 500,000.01 and is rejected with RequiresTwoApprovers.

## 2.x Phase 2: two-approver rule
- [ ] Approvals list on the invoice records each approver by user id.
- [ ] Second-approver logic enforces the Director-only second approval and does not allow duplicate users.
- [ ] Replace the interim rule and its test T6 with the final above-500,000 behavior.
- [ ] UI message when the invoice stays Pending after a first approval is surfaced to the user.
- [ ] Unit tests U1 to U12 cover the two-approver flow, precedence, unchanged-state checks, and boundary behavior.

# Proposal: add-role-approval-limits

## Summary

Add role-based invoice approval limits so that Manager and Director approvals are constrained by amount and by the required approval structure. The change keeps the business rules in the domain layer, ensures rejected attempts do not mutate the invoice, and enforces that the second approver on large invoices must be a Director.

## Why

The current approval flow does not distinguish between roles or approval limits. This creates an inconsistency where a user can approve beyond the intended role authority and where large invoices can be approved without the required second reviewer.

## Goals

- Enforce single-approver role limits for Manager and Director users.
- Reject non-approvers and invalid invoice states without mutating the invoice.
- Require two distinct approvers for invoice amounts above 500,000, with the second approver being a Director.
- Preserve unchanged invoice state on any rejected approval attempt.

## Non-goals

- No creator-cannot-approve rule.
- No currency handling.
- No delegation or audit logging.
- No persistence changes.
- No new invoice status values.

## Design intent

The domain will own a pure approval policy and the `ApprovalService` will orchestrate validation and mutation. Controllers will map domain results to existing HTTP errors, and the UI will surface rejection messages in an alert element. Approval data will be tracked on the invoice as a list of approvers, with duplicate user-id checks performed case-insensitively.

## Summary

Add role-based invoice approval limits so that Manager and Director approvals are constrained by amount and by the required approval structure. The change keeps the business rules in the domain layer, ensures rejected attempts do not mutate the invoice, and enforces that the second approver on large invoices must be a Director.

## Why

The current approval flow does not distinguish between roles or approval limits. This creates an inconsistency where a user can approve beyond the intended role authority and where large invoices can be approved without the required second reviewer.

## Goals

- Enforce single-approver role limits for Manager and Director users.
- Reject non-approvers and invalid invoice states without mutating the invoice.
- Require two distinct approvers for invoice amounts above 500,000, with the second approver being a Director.
- Preserve unchanged invoice state on any rejected approval attempt.

## Non-goals

- No creator-cannot-approve rule.
- No currency handling.
- No delegation or audit logging.
- No persistence changes.
- No new invoice status values.

## Design intent

The domain will own a pure approval policy and the `ApprovalService` will orchestrate validation and mutation. Controllers will map domain results to existing HTTP errors, and the UI will surface rejection messages in an alert element. Approval data will be tracked on the invoice as a list of approvers, with duplicate user-id checks performed case-insensitively.
